detailed_description: Live-action 1970s Shaw Brothers historical studio cinema, ancient Troy, saturated 35mm film colors, theatrical hard light, practical timber and stone sets. One enormous hollow wooden Trojan horse, visibly made from timber planks with the same golden bronze bands, mounted on the same four-wheeled timber platform. Its four rigid wooden legs never walk, its head never moves, and its wheels rotate only while pulled. One rectangular hinged hatch on its camera-facing belly and one wooden ladder. The Greek leader is the bearded short-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a red cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and no shield. His companion is the clean-shaven curly-dark-haired man in engraved bronze armor and a blue cloak, with one sword sheathed at his right hip and one round bronze shield strapped to his back. They use free hands to climb. Keep faces, hair, armor, cloak colors, equipment ownership and horse construction consistent. [Shot 1] Daylight. Wide establishing shot outside the arched stone gate of Troy. A few Trojan workers in simple tan tunics pull ropes, slowly rolling the enormous rigid wooden horse into the city. The camera tracks right at ground level, showing wooden wheels rotating and the horse passing under the arch. The hatch is completely shut. All Greek soldiers remain hidden inside, invisible. overall_soundscape: Ropes creak, wooden wheels rumble on stone, sandals scuff, distant city ambience. No dialogue or music. non_diegetic_music: None.
